overview: Porth Chapel is a small, secluded cove near St Levan, tucked between Porthcurno and Porthgwarra on the far south-west tip of Cornwall. It’s famous for its pale shell sand, clear turquoise water and granite cliffs, and because it’s harder to reach, it’s much quieter than its neighbours.
Above the beach is St Levan’s Holy Well, and the remains of a tiny chapel that may date back as far as the 8th century.

expect.title: The cove
expect.text: Pale shell-sand beach and clear water framed by granite cliffs.

expect.title: Wildlife
expect.text: Look out for grey seals, dolphins and seabirds such as fulmars and shags.

expect.title: St Levan’s Well
expect.text: A holy well above the beach, still used for baptisms at the parish church.

goodToKnow.label: Getting down
goodToKnow.text: It’s tricky to get to, which is exactly why it stays so quiet.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: There are no facilities at the beach; Porthcurno has a café and toilets nearby.

week.slot: Two hours to half a day
week.text: A quiet alternative to busy Porthcurno, ideally visited at low to mid tide. Combine it with the Minack Theatre just above and a walk along the coast path to Porthgwarra.

pairWith.why: the bigger, busier beach next door
the clifftop theatre just along the path
a tiny fishing cove to the west

tips: Wear sturdy shoes for the path down and take everything you need with you.
